Consequently, it is vitally important to detect and isolate a fault at the right time in these systems. To do so, here, unknown input observers (UIO) are proposed for robust fault detection and isolation of actuators and sensors in buildings. For the proof of concept, a three-story structure with magnetorheological (MR) dampers is taken into account. Via designing these observers, each faulty actuator and/or sensor is detected and isolated. Here, the LQR controller is also used to facilitate an optimal control strategy over the system. The obtained simulation results utter the acceptable accuracy of the proposed method in the detection of fault (time and location) and the robustness of the fault detection method against external disturbances.

articleTitle: Reforming Architecture and Loss Function of Artificial Neural Networks in Binary Classification Problems
abstract: Artificial neural networks (ANNs), implied models of the biological human brain's neuron, have now a long history as prime techniques in machine learning and computational intelligence with a wide range of applications, and are of great interest thanks to their great success. Classification is one of the most populous realms of research in ANNs with a vast and growing literature. Our innovation is to revolutionize loss function for ANNs, in accordance with a novel architecture for the last layer of the neural net (NN), that empowers them to apply dynamic thresholding while deciding the label of a sample based on its probability-of-belonging values; hence, to model complexities of the data more discriminatingly and attain better quantitative results. Although we established our approach through mathematical argument particularly for binary classification, the concept and formulation are entirely and purposefully generalizable to multiclass classification problems.

articleTitle: Takagi-Sugeno (TS) Fuzzy model-basedobserver design for glucose-insulin system in diabetes type 1: An LMI approach
abstract: Paper This proposes a Takagi-Sugeno fuzzy model-based observer for glucose-insulin system for estimating the states of glucose-insulin system in diabetes type 1. In this approach, the Takagi-Sugeno (TS) fuzzy modeling is employed and linear matrix inequalities (LMIs) are utilized to derive the estimation conditions. Nonlinear minimal Bergman model as a description of glucose-insulin process in type 1 diabetes is considered.

articleTitle: Novel High Q Single Layer Bridgeless RF MEMS Inductors
abstract: This paper presents the design and simulation of a single layer RF MEMS-based inductors. The inductors are shown in three different shapes. The proposed inductors are made using a standard fabrication method called metal MUMPs design. There is just one possible conductive metal layer in this standard method, so there is not any chance to make a bridge for the inductor. The proposed inductors do not need any bridge in their structure. The simulation results show high-quality factor and reasonable return loss and insertion loss compared to conventional inductors.

articleTitle: State Estimation of Time Varying Fractional Singular Systems
abstract: This paper presents a linear filtering for the stochastic fractional-order singular (FOS) models in discrete time varying (TV) cases. The filter is established by using deterministic argumentation in an entirely independent way besides the stochastic analysis, and the recursive algorithm is derived by solving a well-organized data-fitting estimate problem of complete state samples given the measurements for TV and noise correlated cases. By presenting a numerical simulation, we try to verify our hypothesis and results obtained throughout this paper.

articleTitle: Wireless Energy Harvesting and Self-Energy Recycling in a Full-Duplex MIMO Relay Network with Interference Alignment
abstract: We investigate the performance of utilizing a full-duplex (FD) wireless powered relay to facilitate transmission between base-station (BS) and a distant user in a small cell. Relay employs the power splitting (PS) method to harvest its necessary power from the interference and residual self-interference (RSI) signals. Aiming at maximizing the transmission rate of the distant user, we derive a closed-form solution for relay optimal PS ratio. Moreover, we apply the interference alignment (IA) technique with the Max-SINR approach to jointly eliminate the interferences, including the RSI signal at relay's information processing unit, and maximize the transmission rate. At last, simulations illustrate the rate gain of the proposed scheme over the benchmark schemes.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of a Polarization Converter Based on Graphene Metasurfaces
abstract: In this paper, a polarization converter (PC) in the mid-infrared frequency range is presented. The considered structure consists of a polymer of substrate backed by a gold layer and a graphene layer which laid on top of it. The designed PC works in the bandwidth of 33.67THz to 35.98THz. Furthermore, the operation frequency of the metasurface can be tunned by adjusting the bias voltage applied to the graphene.

articleTitle: Target and Image Elevation Angles Separation Algorithm for Low-Angle Tracking with Monopulse Antenna
abstract: The multipath phenomenon causes error in elevation angle tracking operation of low altitude targets. Returning signals from the target after reflecting from the surface enter the antenna main beam. In such circumstances, the surface acts like a mirror and creates an image of the real target beneath the surface. Multipath effect elimination is a major challenge in tracking systems. In an attempt to decrease the multipath effects, the authors extended the elevation geometric mean method and presented the target and image elevation angles separation algorithm with monopulse antenna. The proposed method presents two equations for calculating the real and image elevation angles. These two equations are expressing the summation and the multiplication of the target and its image angle. This method presents low computational complexity and simple implementation on the monopulse tracking system. The computer simulation results show that the proposed method is able to mitigate the multipath effect and estimate the elevation angle with high accuracy.

articleTitle: Functional classification of neurons in mouse hippocampus based on spike waveforms in extracellular recordings
abstract: Neurons are functionally classified into inhibitory and excitatory categories based on the influence they have on the firing rates of their postsynaptic neurons after being stimulated. Although assessing the firing rates of postsynaptic neurons is the main way of this categorization, it is very hard in real cases. Due to the lack of a labelled dataset with inhibitory and excitatory neurons, past studies have been conducted to investigate the feasibility of this categorization based on clustering some features of the spike waveforms and evaluating the results by physiological evidence. However, there is still the lack of a classification study in order to do this categorization by using features of spike waveforms and different classifiers. This is what we addressed in this paper based on a recent labeled dataset of mouse hippocampus neurons. We extracted nine different features from neuron spikes. Then we investigated the significance of difference of each feature between inhibitory and excitatory groups using Wilcoxon rank-sum-test and also evaluated the effectiveness of all possible feature subsets for classification using KNN, LDA, and SVM classifiers. The highest average classification accuracy was %96.96 obtained by using SVM with RBF kernel and five features. However, KNN yielded %96.08 average accuracy by using just one feature which was Peak amplitude asymmetry. In addition, Peak amplitude asymmetry, Peak-to-trough ratio, and Duration between peaks selected more in the optimum feature subsets using different classifiers. Generally, we concluded the features obtained from waveform spikes and simple common classifiers can effectively classify neurons into inhibitory and excitatory categories.

articleTitle: Propagation delay and stability analysis of MWCNT and MLGNR interconnects
abstract: By utilizing an equivalent single conductor model, the performance of MWCNT bundle and MLGNR interconnects at global lengths is compared in terms of propagation delay and frequency stability. Results show that MLGNR interconnects can outperform MWCNT bundle counterpart (i.e. have shorter propagation delay) if properly doped and placed over enough smooth substrate surfaces. In terms of stability, MLGNR interconnects at global lengths are always more stable than their MWCNT bundle counterpart.

articleTitle: Application of Rogowski Coil for Improving Security of Transformer Differential Protection
abstract: This paper presents a simple method for improving the security and reliability of Harmonic Blocking Algorithms (HBAs) in differential protection of power transformers. In the proposed method, instead of using conventional Current Transformer (CT), Rogowski Coil Sensor (RCS) is utilized for sensing the transformer currents. Based on a theoretic analysis, it is shown that the use of RCS increases the margin between the second harmonic ratio levels of the energization and fault conditions, thereby increasing the HBAs security. Besides, the use of RCS has the additional advantage of eliminating the problem of CT saturation, which might cause malfunction of the differential relay. The validity of the proposed technique is demonstrated by evaluating extensive test cases in different operating conditions, which are recorded by digital simulations in PSCAD/EMTDC software. Overall, the results demonstrate that the proposed approach improves the security of HBAs by about 6.8%.

articleTitle: Speech Enhancement Using NMF based on Hierarchical Deep Neural Networks with Joint Learning
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel method which includes autoencoder and deep neural networks (DNNs) in a hierarchal structure for speech enhancement. In this method, at first, two parallel autoencoders are employed to obtain the nonnegative matrix factorization (NMF) parameters of speech and noise in a nonlinear mapping. After that, by using the spectrum of noisy speech as the input of the encoder portion of the autoencoders, the outputs of the encoders are calculated and utilized as the input of DNNs in the next hierarchies to further enhance the speech spectrum more efficiently. Also, the last three hierarchies including the decoder portion of autoencoders and the DNN will be trained in a joint learning scenario to improve the results. The proposed method is evaluated on TIMIT corpus with perceptual-evaluation-of-speech-quality (PESQ) and frequency-weighted-segmental-signal-to-noise-ratio (fwSNRseg) criterions. The obtained results show a significant improvement in both seen and unseen noises compared to baselines.

articleTitle: Integrating Demand Response Programs in Co-Optimization of Electricity and Gas Systems
abstract: The raise of gas-based generators in the electricity systems to compensate for the intermittent nature of renewable energies has created interaction between gas and electricity systems. As well as, the advent of power to gas (P2G) technology has strengthened interactions. In this work, a co-optimization framework for electricity and gas systems taking into account P2G technology is proposed. Additionally, electricity and gas demand response programs integrated into the model to decrease the gas system effect on power system operation. A test system is employed in order to evaluate the proposed framework. The numerical results of the test system verify the efficiency of the proposed framework in the co-optimization of two systems.

articleTitle: The effect of consuming energy on the output power of a photovoltaic tracking system, case study: urban area in Tehran
abstract: Solar trackers are an ideal tool for improving the efficiency of panels. In this paper, First, we design and implement two photovoltaic systems, one with a fixed angle and the other with a dual-axis solar tracker. Then we investigate the effects of time step on tracker power output. By decreasing the tracker time step, the tracking becomes more accurate and the number of moves increases. As a result, the power consumption of controllers and motors increase. To investigate the relationship between the optimal time step of the tracker and its energy consumption, experiments were conducted in a residential location in Tehran. Experimental results show that the appropriate time step for two axes is 20 minutes and for one axis is 10 minutes.

articleTitle: Balanced Application Scheduling for Process Variation Influenced Chip Multiprocessors
abstract: Within-die process variations in chip-multiprocessors cause wide variation in the distribution of frequency and power consumption between similar cores. In such condition, considering variations in task allocation and power management algorithms is crucial. Among various methods proposed to improve performance and reduce power consumption in variation-influenced chip-multiprocessors, two of them are more popular: variation-aware application scheduling and per-core dynamic voltage and frequency scaling (DVFS). However, none of the proposed methods guarantees load balancing in chip-multiprocessors and as a result, appropriate distribution of power in task allocation cannot be achieved by these methods. In this paper we propose an algorithm which intelligently maps (and remaps) applications into cores considering their variations. Moreover, proposed power management algorithm maximizes the overall performance at a given power budget. For power management, low resolution DVFS is used to decrease algorithm overhead. Additionally, the algorithm is “balanced” to avoid hotspots on the chip. The proposed method is tested on a special-purpose simulator based on E3S data-set Experimental results show that the algorithm achieves significant improvement in terms of power distribution and fair application scheduling compared to the other methods.

articleTitle: An Effective Signature for Detection of Flicker Sources in Transmission Networks Using Fast Fourier Transform
abstract: Before taking any action for reduction of flicker negative impacts, it is essential to identify the main contributors of flicker in the network. This paper proposes an effective signature, by which one can determine whether a flicker source is connected to a specified bus of the transmission network or not. Hence, it will be useful for rectifying disagreements between network operator and industrial consumers about flicker generation. The proposed signature is extracted from complex power angle versus frequency diagram for a specified bus of the network. This diagram is achieved by performing fast Fourier transform (FFT) on three-phase measurements of the bus voltage and load feeder current. Based on simulation results presented for a standard test system, it is shown that in case a flicker source is connected to a specified bus, this diagram has mirror symmetry around the system operating frequency. Moreover, relative extrema of this diagram occur at side frequencies that differ from the network operating frequency by the flicker source frequency. Hence, the proposed signature is also helpful for evaluating the frequency content of the flicker source.

articleTitle: A Wideband Two-Stage Double Balanced Mixing Structure for Mapping the In-Out Overlapped Frequency Bands
abstract: A wideband two-stage mixing structure is proposed for multi band frequency mapping of the subsystems with overlapped input and output frequency bands. The proposed structure circumvents the image and leakage problems which are the major challenges in applications with overlapped input and output frequency bands. In such cases, the image and leaked harmonics cannot be filtered because they are inherently located in the working band. The challenges are overcome by using the proposed two-stage frequency mapping structure with a fixed and a variable local oscillator in the first and second stages of the mixers, respectively. By applying the proposed structure followed by the instructions to set the variables, filtering requirements become more relaxed. In addition, GaAs MMIC double balanced mixers are employed in this design to perform multi tune mixing. We have designed and investigated a test board as a real case of overlapped frequency mapping. It was fabricated on the RF Rogers-4003c substrate for the test and verification of the proposed idea. The test board can map any frequency band from 1 GHz to 4 GHz to the output frequency band 1 GHz to 5 GHz. The total gain variation across the whole frequency band was observed to be less than 5 dB.

articleTitle: Low-Profile and High Efficient Artificial Magnetic Conductor Metasurface for X-Band Applications
abstract: A low profile artificial magnetic conductor metasurface has been proposed in this paper. The simple structure of the unitcell and small size of the structure, (0.13λ×0.13λ), in 8.8 GHz makes it suitable for wireless communication systems operating in X-band. The simulated and measured results with good agreements have been presented and discussed in detail.

articleTitle: AIS Link Budget Design and Probability of Detection Analysis in Multi User System
abstract: The Automatic Identification System (AIS) was introduced By International Maritime Organization (IMO) in 2000 for the first time to increase the maritime safety. In the past several decades, Satellite Automatic Identification System (S-AIS) has played an important role in maritime communications. Due to this subject, this paper mainly focused on AIS link budget calculation, channel load and throughput system for the vessels near IRAN maritime boundaries. The aim of our work is to examine the effects of distance and angle between satellites to ship for computing the probability of detection. An experimental model for the S-AIS system has been evaluated based on Systems (Satellite) Tool Kit (STK) software. Also, the probability of detection versus number of interference with different signal to interference power ratio in satellite has been extracted, numerically.

articleTitle: Interference Alignment in a Frequency Selective X Channel with Blind Transmitters, Relay and Limited Channel Extensions
abstract: Interference alignment (IA) is a powerful interference controlling technique that can eliminate limited interferences in restricted bandwidth systems. In this paper, IA is applied in a frequency selective X channel, and A relay is deployed to obtain more realistic results. The problems of infinite symbol extensions and CSIT requirement are overcome by using a relay with ability to precode the messages. In the assumed relay assisted X channel, all transmitters are considered to be blind, and the optimal DoF at low SNR regime is achievable. The number of relay antennas, which makes IA implementation possible are derived. The simulation results show sum-mean-square-error (SMSE) converges and the small number of subcarriers is required. For example, 5000 users can exchange their data over 10000 subcarriers over an X channel.

articleTitle: A New Algorithm for Maximizing Total Big Data Flow in a Cloud Radio Access Network
abstract: In this paper, we propose a new algorithm to maximize the total down link Big Data flow in terms of total number of transmitted packets per millisecond for cloud radio access networks (C-RANs). We formulate the above problem using the C-RAN graph. The fairness is the implicit objective of this problem. The proposed algorithm solves this problem by selecting paths of the Big Data transmission. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm achieves better total Big Data flows, as well as better fairness.

articleTitle: Resilient Control Strategy for Detection and Mitigation of Disruptions in Microgrids
abstract: A distributed power system, including several microgrids, is always vulnerable to attacks which can result in malfunctioning. In order to protect the system from such attacks, the problem of resilient consensus in microgrids has been discussed in this paper. A network of microgrids as a multiagent system is considered in the presence of misbehaving agents that might make updates arbitrarily. By using the quantization algorithm, each agent will take integer values under directed communication links. The normal agents aim to reach consensus while the malicious ones become isolated. This can be achieved by the use of a special approach of mean subsequence reduced algorithms (MSR) in which all normal agents ignore extreme values received by their neighbors before updating their states. The agents are studied under synchronous and asynchronous updates. Moreover, a controller is suggested that can make the system reach consensus even though, the normal agents only can access their neighbors' values with time-delays. Finally, numerical examples and simulation results are provided.

articleTitle: Reflect Array Antenna with Isoflux Beam for Satellite Application
abstract: In this paper a low loss reflective surface for beam shaping with wide bandwidth is presented. In this reflective surface an orthogonal polarization is achieved with the use of a metallic symmetric unitcell. Simple fabrication, adjustment of reflective phase and low loss are the main advantages of this unitcell. With the use of this unitcell, a reflective surface with isoflux beam for satellite applications in X-band frequency is designed and the simulation and optimization results are presented. The bandwidth of the presented unitcell for designed beam is above the 120%.

articleTitle: Identification of Epilepsy utilizing Hilbert Transform and SVM based Classifier
abstract: Epilepsy is a persistent neurological condition of the brain in which the activity of the brain goes out of normal state. Classification and Analysis of EEG signal is the early approach for epilepsy diagnosis. During this paper, we have a tendency to propose an EEG signal classification approach based on Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifier. In extracting features from the raw EEG data we applied the Hilbert Transform method and used its coefficients. Then, after the PCA dimension reduction a two-class SVM classifier is used for EEG signals automatic classification, one class for healthy subjects and another for subjects with epilepsy. In SVM classifier we need to divide the EEG signals into a training dataset and testing dataset for classification. We have used five sets of EEG signals which are publicly accessible on EEG time series database. The evaluation and comparison of SVM based classifier with two other classification methods such as KNN and LVQ based classifier was done. The average classification accuracy of our study is 95.33%.

articleTitle: T2FPID Load Frequency Control for a two-area Power System Considering Input Delay
abstract: In this study, a novel type-2 fuzzy (T2F) PID (T2FPID) controller is proposed for the load frequency control (LFC) of a nonlinear 2-area power system which suffering from input delay. It is clear that the input delay can degrade the functioning of the plant. In the T2FPID controller, appropriate tuning of output scaling factor (OSF) can improve the functioning of the plant, especially in handling the delay and uncertainties. In this study, a Lyapunov-Krasovskii (L-K) functional is utilized to figure out the stability of the designed LFC, and the tuning laws are obtained for the adaptive parameters using this functional. To illustrate the usefulness of the suggested adaptive T2FPID controller, a comparison to a non-adaptive T2FPID controller is given for a 2-area system with input delay.

articleTitle: Visual-Inertial State Estimation Based on PSO-BPNN UKF
abstract: In recent decades, the integrated Visual-Inertial Odometry (VIO) system has frequently used for accurate and efficient ego-motion estimation of many autonomous vehicles. In order to obtain navigation results by high accuracy in the VIO, Unscented Kalman Filter (UKF) has been proposed as an optimization-based approach by some studies. UKF can overcome the error accumulation and the Jacobian matrixes calculation that they are limitations of Extended KF (EKF). In this paper an improved UKF is presented that it is combined with the combination of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Back Propagation Neural Network (BPNN). In this combined approach, in order to correct the navigation parameters, the prediction values of PSO-BPNN can be used by UKF. The experimental navigation results have been utilized to show the effectiveness of VIO based on PSO-BPNN UKF against the VIO based on traditional UKF in well-known KITTI dataset.

articleTitle: Electrical Conduction in Dense Polycrystalline Rutile at Low frequencies
abstract: The complex ionic-electronic conduction in rutile has been considered for the fabrication of memristive devices with different structures. The memristive features of the device is believed to originate from the motion of the ionized oxygen vacancies within the oxide crystal. Here, we investigate the conduction mechanism in Ti/poly-rutile/Ti devices at low frequencies, wherein the contribution of ionic movement to the charge conduction is significant. The I-V characteristics of the device are recorded by applying triangular voltages ranging from -2 to +2 V at different frequencies in the range of 0.01-100 Hz. Recorded results demonstrate very different I-V plots for voltage sweeping frequencies of 0.01 and 100 Hz. Even after applying compensations for the capacitive current, the device current at 0.01 Hz is significantly larger than that at 100 Hz. The obtained results are described by assuming conductive filament formation within the polycrystalline solid; these filaments provide easy conduction routes which changes the conduction status in the sample.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of an All-Optical Plasmonic Fano Switch
abstract: The optical switch is a crucial component in optical communications that plays an important role in transmitting the optical signal within a photonic circuit. In this paper, an all-optical plasmonic switch composed of five nanodisks made from gold, planted inside SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">z</sub> substrate, based on Fano resonance, has been proposed. The simulation results disclose that the structure can work as an infrared optical switch by adjusting the pump light at 825 nm wavelength. The occurrence of the second Fano resonance (FR) due to the reduction in the distance between nanodisks was reviewed. The two-dimensional simulations using the finite-difference time-domain algorithm are utilized to reveal apparent optical bistability and notable switching mechanism of the signal light. The results show -4.00 dB and -36.84 dB transmissions when the pump is OFF and ON, respectively. As known, in highly integrated optical communication, ultra-small all-optical switches are of great importance. This switch has a nanoscale size of 450 nm×450 nm.

articleTitle: An Analytical Model to Justify the Frequency Dependence of the Photocapacitance Effect in Organic Heterojunction Devices
abstract: The photocapacitance effect in organic heterojunction devices was investigated, revealing that it depends on the measuring frequency. The frequency dispersion was measured for the structure of ITO/CuPc/PTCBI/Al and in order to justify the origin of the frequency dependence, an analytical model was introduced based on the emission and capture rates of traps. On the basis of the model, traps lifetime could be decreased by exposure to light so that the junction capacitance increases at low frequencies. Furthermore, the degree of density of traps being dominant in either n-type or p-type regions mostly controls the behavior of the dispersion curve.

articleTitle: $Q$-learning Approach for Optimal Power Dispatch of Microgrid
abstract: In this paper, the power dispatch of grid-connected microgrid (MG) using Q-learning has been studied. The MG is considered as multi-agent system and all distributed generations and customers are considered as self-interested agents. The aim of these agents is to maximize their own profit in MG. Considering the uncertainty of output power of renewable generation and fluctuations of customers' consumption, a Q-learning approach has been proposed for optimal power dispatch of generation resource and demand side management of customers. In the proposed model, the optimal amount of power production of MG sources as well as the amount of power exchange with the main grid for 24-hour period is determined. Simulation results show the effectiveness of proposed approach.

articleTitle: Road Scene Image Segmentation Based on Feature Fusion
abstract: Image segmentation in machine vision is a significant step to get a holistic image understanding of the captured scene. Region-based, edge-based, clustering, learning-based methods are image segmentation approaches and there are plenty of methods for each one. Beside these methods, image fusion as a branch of data fusion is related to machine vision by enhancing image in different ways and levels (pixel, feature and decision). In autonomous vehicles (A V) and Advanced assistant driver systems (ADAS) cameras are important sensors those widely used to control and navigate system. Front view camera gives an image from frontal scene containing different objects that should be processed during driving phase. Making a good segmentation from the scene helps AVs or ADAS systems to tackle their duties. In this research, we have used fusing different segmentation and object Classification in order to get a better perception of surrounding area. On the other hand, the system should complete all process in fraction of a second, so it is so important to reach the best execution time for A V s' real time applications. K-Mean and Fuzzy C-Mean (FCM) are clustering methods and also two methods for fusing different specific parts (features) of image to a class or fused decision in high level data fusion. There for, we will reach to a segmented image in which background and foreground are completely separated.

articleTitle: Enhancing Multi-layer Multicast Routing in Wireless Mesh Networks by Exploiting Wireless Broadcast Advantage
abstract: This paper investigates the problem of multicast communication in wireless mesh networks (WMNs). The proposed algorithm uses the multi-layer scheme, in which the multicast data is encoded into multiple layers, to handle bandwidth heterogeneous receivers. Additionally, it exploits two techniques to increase the number of obtained layers by the receivers, namely network coding and wireless broadcast advantage (WBA). Incorporating WBA necessitates determining the children of the nodes, which complicates the design. To solve the problem in polynomial time, the network is partitioned into some groups, and each group is considered independently. The grouping technique is also used to determine the obtained layers by each receiver. The simulations demonstrate that our algorithm considerably outperforms the previous approaches.

articleTitle: Parkinson's Disease Detection Using Dynamic Writing Traces Warping
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a kind of brain damage arising from diminishing in dopamine production. As conventional diagnostic methods are time-consuming, expensive and somewhat subjective, there is a need to propose a cost-effective and reliable detection system. Since one of the most prominent features of PD is impaired performance of motor skills, online handwriting analysis can provide a useful tool for detection of disease. In this study, a nonlinear method based on dynamic writing traces warping (DWTW) in combination with support vector machine classifier was developed. It was evaluated on a database of 32 healthy and 29 PD infected samples. Further, effects of eight handwriting tasks were investigated. The proposed method achieved high average accuracy rate of 88.33%, sensitivity of 86.43% and specificity of 89.5%. This study demonstrated the capability of DWTW features as a cost effective and discriminative measure for diagnosis of PD.

articleTitle: Large-Capacitive-Load OTA With NMOS Input and PMOS Input Current Boosting Cells
abstract: This paper presents a low-power and high gain-bandwidth (GBW) OTA for large capacitive load applications. The proposed OTA utilizes four differential small-signal current boosting cells to increase DC gain and GBW. In this single stage OTA design, two different small-signal current enhancers with NMOS and PMOS inputs are used. This G<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sub>-boosting cells are designed based on the recycling and double-folded structures and have higher current gain with low power consumption. The proposed OTA with 15 nF capacitive load was simulated in a 0.18 μm technology. The simulation results show that the DC gain is 100 dB at the supply voltage of 0.75 V, GBW is 1.42 MHz and phase margin is 57°. The current consumption is 13.35 μA including all bias and common mode feedback circuits.

articleTitle: Prediction of the Brain Surprise in Sequences of Oddball Stimuli
abstract: Certain features of the Event Related Potential (ERP) signal such as the P300 and N200 components are known to reflect the surprise of the brain when encountering unlikely samples in a sequence of stimuli. In this paper, we propose a method to learn the amplitude of these components for an arbitrary random stimuli sequence. First, a Fisher optimization method is developed for binary prediction of the P300 occurrence. Then, a Generalized Linear Method (GLM) is employed to predict the amplitude of the P300 component. The proposed method is applied to an auditory oddball experiment with recorded Electroencephalogram (EEG) data. Both developed methods are shown to yield promising results with an acceptable prediction error.

articleTitle: A Novel Horn Antenna with a Bed of Nails with High Gain and Low Side Lobes
abstract: The objective of this article is to offer a novel technique for reducing SLL on the E-plane, which has been theoretically investigated. The suggested antenna is a novel horn antenna with a bed of nails in the E-plane. To show better operation of this antenna than both conventional and corrugated horn antennas, the results of all three antennas are compared. It is shown that the nails placed in the walls of the modified horn antenna tapers the fields over the E-plane walls which reduces the side-lobe-level (SLL) in the E plane. Besides, the suggested horn antenna with nails has a more symmetric radiation pattern than the conventional and corrugated horn antennas. In addition, it has lower weight than the corrugated horn antenna and higher weight than the conventional horn antenna.

articleTitle: Fusion of Amplitude and Complex Domains based on Deep Neural Networks for Speech Enhancement
abstract: Most of the recent works on speech enhancement has estimated the domain of clean spectrum and directly added noisy phase to the estimated domain without any processing. Nowadays, most of the phase-aware systems in speech processing are made up of using both real and imaginary parts of speech spectrum rather than the raw phase. In this paper, we propose a novel approach by the fusion of two deep methods for speech enhancement in the complex domain. This method combines the output of two deep neural networks (DNN) that estimate the complex ideal ratio mask (cIRM) and the amplitude of clean speech with a new logarithmic-based decision rule. This fusion rule which has been proposed according to psychoacoustics findings and spectrogram observations produces a complementary structure. Hence, it is capable of using the advantages of both amplitude and complex mask estimators in each time-frequency region. The above method, when evaluated on TIMIT corpus, outperforms the perceptual evaluation of speech quality (PESQ) compared to other approaches especially in unseen noise conditions showing the better generalization of the proposed architecture.

articleTitle: Fabrication of non-volatile resistive switching memory based on Graphene oxide and PEDOT:PSS mixture
abstract: In the current article, we describe a resistive switching random access memory based on a homogenized mixture of Graphene oxide(GO) and PEDOT:PSS(PP). To make a comparison, memory devices with GO and PP were fabricated and characterized too. It is found that blending previous materials significantly change the hysteresis properties of memories in a good way. In our experiment, the structure Al/GO-PP(1:1)/ITO demonstrated good switching behavior with approximately 10<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> on/off current ratio, low 3V set/reset voltage, high 6000 sec retention time, symmetrical hysteresis curve and small energy consumption.

articleTitle: Determination of Floquet's Modes in Graphene-Based Periodic Structures Using Method of Lines
abstract: In this work, the Method of Lines (MoL) is proposed for the analysis of anisotropic graphene-based periodic structures for the first time. This method is based on the Floquet's theorem and stable impedance/admittance transformation. Using Floquet's theorem, we equivalent the periodic structure with a transmission line. Due to this equivalence, an eigenvalue problem is developed. Floquet's modes of the periodic structure are the solutions of this eigenvalue problem. To verify the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method, numerical results for different graphene-based periodic waveguides are presented and compared with those of commercial EM solvers which are in excellent agreement.

articleTitle: Logic Encryption to Prevent Trojan Insertion with Dual-Function Gates
abstract: The outsourcing of integrated circuits (IC) makes some of the vulnerabilities and enable the adversary to reverse engineering attack, IP piracy, overproduction, counterfeiting or hardware Trojan (HT) insertion throughout the supply chain of the IC. The attacker by inserting the hardware Trojan can destroy normal operation in IC, or steal sensitive information from the design. Nowadays the prevention of IP piracy and HT insertion is an important issue in hardware security. Logic encryption as part of Design for Hardware Trust (DFHT) techniques, applies key-gates in order to encrypt the logic of the chip. Therefore if the key inputs are correct the chip has normal function otherwise function is wrong, this work prevention of IP piracy. Furthermore, in some cases of logic encryption techniques, the rare signals that are a good place for insert an HT can be reduced. Therefore, if the HT is inserted in the chip by functional tests can be detected. In this article, a new key-gate that has a double-function is designed to prevent HT insertion as well as preventing from IP piracy. In this paper, by reducing the rare signals and reducing the signals with low observability, prevent HT insertion also, this type of key-gates is resistant to reverse engineering more than the previously designed key-gates. This key-gates has overhead less than insertion based method with XOR and XNOR key-gates.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of a High-Efficiency Inverse Class-F Power Amplifier for S-Band Application
abstract: In this paper, a high efficiency Class-F<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> power amplifier (PA) for the S-Band application is presented. The load network of the proposed Class-F<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> PA satisfies the impedance requirements at f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>, 2f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>, and 3f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> frequency. The simulation results verify the analytical results. This power amplifier has been designed based on GaN HEMT device CGH40035F at a frequency band from 2.2-2.4 GHz. The results show drain efficiency and output power higher than 65% and 44.6 dBm, respectively. The obtained results show that the desired characteristics for the proposed PA have been obtained.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Predictive Controller Design Based on Subspace Identification And Bilinear Modeling
abstract: In this paper, Model Predictive Control (MPC) extended to a subclass of non-linear systems based on the subspace approach using the bilinear model. The merit of this approach is that MPC controller design is obtained directly from subspace matrices, which are identified based on system input/output data. This method is useful for unknown systems. Linear controllers cannot describe the practical systems because the practical systems are non-linear, so we proposed the MPC controller design based on the bilinear subspace model.

articleTitle: An ultra low voltage subthreshold standard cell based memories for IoT applications
abstract: In this paper, we have designed an ultra low voltage standard cell based memory (SCM) in the subthreshold domain. The SCM has been synthesized, placed and routed based on an ultra low voltage full custom standard cell library using 130 nm process technology, functional for subthreshold supply voltages as low as 140 mV, which is well below the supply voltages reported in the previous works of SCMs. This SCM has been designed based on the standard D-latch which holds data at a supply voltage as low as 170 mV. The designed SCM is functional for a temperature range of 27-50 °C applicable for implantable biomedical systems requiring small memory capacity. According to the simulations from the extracted netlist, the energy per bit access at Vdd=200 mV and 333 kHz frequency, suitable for many loT applications, is 1.54 fJ.

articleTitle: Analyzing the effects of impressed current on the behavior of STT-MTJ devices through shaping the PDF of the magnetization vector
abstract: The states of the magneto resistive tunnel junction (MTJ) devices are determined by the direction of their magnetization vector. The Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert (LLG) differential equation governs the trajectory of the magnetization vector. For the low current values or the switching pulses that have small durations, the end tip of this vector points randomly to somewhere in the 4π [Steradian] of the spherical coordinate. To find the probability density function (PDF) of this distribution, the Fokker-Planck stochastic differential equation (SDE) should be solved. In this paper the PDF of the spin-transfer torque (STT) MTJ s are analyzed. It is shown that by properly shaping the current, one can shape the PDF of the magnetization vector. Hence, the state of the device can be switched completely or can be kept in an uncertain situation with the same probability of switching or non-switching to occur. Biasing the device in such a way that its state become unclear will have applications in designing pseudo number generators or cryptography circuits.

articleTitle: A Novel mapping for visual to auditory sensory substitution
abstract: Visual information can be converted into audio stream via sensory substitution devices in order to give visually impaired people the chance of perception of their surrounding easily and simultaneous to performing everyday tasks. In this study, visual environmental features namely, coordinate, type of objects and their size are assigned to audio features related to music tones such as frequency, time duration and note permutations. Results demonstrated that this new method has more training time efficiency in comparison with our previous method named VBTones which sinusoidal tones were applied. Moreover, results in blind object recognition for real objects was achieved 88.05 on average.

articleTitle: A Graph Theoretic Based Feature Selection Method Using Multi Objective PSO
abstract: Feature selection is a dimensionality reduction method known as a main step in data mining and machine learning. The aim of feature selection is to remove redundant and unrelated features. In recent years several feature selection methods based on graph theory and social networking techniques have been proposed .In this study, a feature selection approach based on multi objective PSO algorithm and social network techniques is presented. In the proposed method, Fisher score, node centrality and edge centrality are used to construct the fitness function in order to present a multi objective particle swarm optimization (PSO) approach. The proposed method run over a variety of datasets and the results are compared with the well-known filter-based feature selection methods. The results show that the proposed method is effective and the performance of the proposed method better than other methods in some cases.

articleTitle: A Weighted Distance Learning Method for Graph Classification
abstract: A weighted distance-learning method is used, in this paper, to optimize the accuracy of Nearest-Neighbour classifier for a graph-based data set. This algorithm tunes the weights of the training instances to minimize an analytical approximation of the classification-error on the training data. With this method, not only the distance function, which has an effective role in the performance of classifier, is tuned, but also a prototype reduction is achieved as a side effect to reduce both of time and memory complexity of the classifier. This efficiency is more important in the case of having graph instances, because computing the distance of a query graph with each prototype graph is a time-consuming process due to isomorphism. By applying the proposed method on IAM, a benchmark graph dataset, the uniformly good behaviour of the proposed method is presented having results competitive with the related methods.

articleTitle: Signal Detection Improvement Using Bottom Up Wavelet Algorithm in QAM Modulation Reception
abstract: Quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM) is one the common modulation used in digital communications. The major problem of communication systems in transferring data is the additive channel noise which corrupts the underlying curve. Until now, techniques that have been applied to mitigate this problem, such as using parity bit, ..., are mainly intended for implementation at the transmitter end and before the signal is modulated. Obviously had no effect on signal noise in receiver. In this paper, a new block is inserted in the receiving path for alleviating this problem. The block acts as a decision maker that would present a pure signal at the input of the A/D stage. The performance of the introduced block is based on the method of second generation wavelet. The most important part in this method is the proper choice of an appropriate base function, designed according to the input signal, it means not use of single wavelet. Specific wavelets are designed for each noisy signal to achieve the best adaption with data in every scale and location.

articleTitle: Economic and Environmental Analysis of DER Integration in Smart Homes with Development of RTP and DLC
abstract: The problem of distributed energy resources (DER) integration in smart homes is evaluated in this paper. This has been done by considering the energy cost savings of smart home and environmental pollution reduction. The DER utilized in the study are photovoltaic (PV) panel, wind turbine (WT) and energy storage system (ESS). The Pareto optimality is employed to solve the two-objective optimization problem. In addition, demand response (DR) programs including real-time pricing (RTP) and direct load control (DLC) are applied in this research. In other words, smart home residents respond to price signals as well as designed incentives. Loads are classified into two groups based on their responsibility. The percentage of loads that respond to these signals and incentives are responsive loads. It was found that, regarding environmental issues, DER integration would be cost-effective. Besides, DR programs reduce energy costs and environmental pollution and increase the cash flow of smart home residents.

articleTitle: Optimal Design of Mid-Infrared Reflective Optical Modulators Based on Electrically Tunable Metasurface
abstract: Mid-infrared modulators based on tunable metasurface enable us to design modulators with high modulation depth (MD) at the desired wavelengths. Regarding the combination of numerous variable parameters affecting the modulator operation, a multi-objective optimization approach was proposed and employed to achieve high MD mid-infrared optical modulators. The multi-objective gray wolf optimizer (MOGWO) is an appropriate method that we are utilizing to maximize the modulators MD. Optimally designed structures, in this work, have demonstrated adequate MD at λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>= 6 μm and λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>= 7 μm. The suggested approach, as a general method, can be used in design optimization of the mid-infrared modulators based on tunable metasurface and tune at any desired wavelength for different usages.

articleTitle: Space-charge-limited current through the electrophoretically formed TiO2/HOPG junction
abstract: Examining the electronic properties of the interface between a semiconductor and the “highly oriented pyrolytic graphite” (HOPG) is an easy, but close, substitute to the investigation of the similar interfaces formed with graphene. Thin layers of TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> are deposited on the freshly cleaved surfaces of HOPG by the electrophoretic deposition (EPD). The process is carried out in the acetone suspensions of sub-100 nm anatase particles using no charging agent. The deposition is anodic. The conductive HOPG substrate is placed on an immersed metal anode. By applying an electric field of 80 V/cm, a layer of anatase is formed on the anode. The produced layers are dried at room temperature and thermally annealed at 350 °C, in air. The samples are examined for the mechanism of electrical conduction through the TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/HOPG junctions by applying varying voltages across the junction and monitoring the current. The obtained current vs voltage diagrams show zero junction barrier. The almost symmetric nonlinearity observed in the I-V diagrams are shown to occur owing to the prevailing space-charge-limited conduction mechanism.

articleTitle: An Experimental Study on the Design & Construction of a Torque Measurement Unit with Tactile Sensors
abstract: This paper presents the state of the art of the design and construction of a torque measurement unit based on a new modification in balancing method. This unit consists of six soft tactile sensors that each include a MEMS barometer covered by silicone rubber. Sensors are mounted in an array under the body of a servo motor to read the force from which motor torque can be obtained. Correct performance of sensor was validated in experimental tests by applying different loads on a Kinco servo motor and comparison of sensor output with value of actual torque obtained from motor driver software. The sensor was able to measure torque with less than 0.1 N.m uncertainty. The main advantage of this torque measurement method is its accuracy, simple construction, precision, real-time measurement and low cost compared to expensive strain gauge based sensors. Due to its soft surface, this torque sensor can be safely employed in human-robot interaction purposes and one can instantly find the force exerted on the environment by the end effector of robot due to the low delay time of the sensors.

articleTitle: Type of Communication between Subpopulations and its Effect on the Multi-objective Search Manager Hybridization Framework
abstract: Sharing information about the best searching point through the communication process between subpopulations is an important step in island-based evolutionary algorithms. This sharing process can be carried out via three models: migration, a best and a model uses both prior models. In this paper, the impact of these three communication models is investigated on the Multi-objective Search Manager (MOSM) which is a recently proposed island-based framework for hybridizing different search strategies aiming to enhance the performance of optimization algorithm in solving multi-objective problems.

articleTitle: A 10 Watts Linear Power Amplifier Using Symmetric Stub Gando Matching Networks
abstract: This paper presents the design and fabrication of a 10 Watts linear power amplifier named “Gando” for the popular cellular frequency spectrum of 2.1 GHz to 2.2 GHz. The high-power amplifier utilizes symmetric stubs layout in input matching network to provide better frequency performance. Working in AB operational class enables this system to maintain the trade-off between linearity and efficiency, while the proper output matching design of this system ensured acceptable harmonic control of the output of the high-power amplifier. Power Added Efficiency of the device is reported about 40 percent while the measured IIP3 of the system is 42.5 dBm.

articleTitle: Sleep arousal events detection using PNN-GBMO classifier based on EEG and ECG signals: A hybrid-learning model
abstract: Foremost sleep event is the sudden change of sleep stages, mainly from deep sleep to light sleep. The notion is very effective in the detection of sleep disorders. In this paper, the detection of arousal events is performed using an automatic analysis of EEG and ECG signals. Unlike previous methods, which rely solely on the detection of sleep stages, early recognition of change in sleep stages can facilitate the progression of some diseases. Detecting the change in sleep stages is a complex process and requires the expertise of a neurologist. Features can be extracted by three fractal descriptors, Lyapunov exponent and cumulatively discrete wavelet transform. A subset of the features is then applied into the probabilistic neural network optimized by Gases Brownian Motion Optimization (GBMO) algorithm. The set of EEG and ECG signals are samples of the SHHS sleep database that have been incorporated into the learning model with some pre-processing. In addition, solving uncertainty problem of responses, repeatability, and convergence to the minimum error are among the strengths of the proposed model. Compared to the conventional feature extraction and classification methods, outputs were obtained that are more acceptable, and the model for two- and four-class states reached averaged errors of less than 2% and 7% with K-fold cross-validation.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Content Caching in Wireless Multi-Tier Heterogeneous Network with ARQ-Transmission
abstract: Content caching at base stations (BSs) and around of users is a hopeful and efficient approach to decrease the effects of traffic growth on wireless networks. In this study, we analyze performance metrics of content caching in a three-tier heterogeneous network (HetNet), including macro base stations (MBSs) for storing contents, small base stations (SBSs) and cache-users (CUs) for storing the most popular contents, where all tiers are distributed according to independent Poisson point processes (PPPs). Specifically, we obtain closed-form expressions for the average outage probability and average delay experienced by the user in case of successful ARQ transmission. In particular, we show that due to the cache memory limitation, the popularity based on content distribution improves the efficiency of the proposed model. Eventually, the efficiency of considered model is illustrated by using numerical results.

articleTitle: Toward a Low-Cost mm-Wave Scalar Network Analyzer Instrumentation
abstract: In this paper, we present a new design and implementation of a mm-wave scalar network analyzer. To achieve this purpose, a spectrum analyzer with tracking generator (DC-18 GHz) is used as a base instrument, and its operating frequency range is extended to W-band (75-110 GHz). The design of the frequency extender is discussed, and preliminary measurements are reported.

articleTitle: Far Field, Suspended Trapping of a Single Dielectric Nanoparticle using Annular Slit-ring Plasmonic Zone-plate Lens
abstract: This paper demonstrates far field, trapping of a single dielectric nanoparticle using a Plasmonic Zone Plate Lens. This is achieved by beaming a linearly polarized light through series of concentric annular slit-rings formed in Gold, leading to creation of a sub-diffraction focal spot in the far field which can be used as a hotspot to trap the nanoparticle in it, suspended. A stable trap is formed in the far field using this structure and a 100-nm Polystyrene particle is successfully trapped using this technique. Forces are calculated in both x and z directions and the stability of the trap is further proved by calculating the potential well for x and z directions at location of the focal spot.

articleTitle: Dual Setting Directional Overcurrent Protection Coordination for Microgrids Considering Single Outage Contingency
abstract: Distributed generation units (DGs) are essential components in microgrids (MGs) and modern distribution systems considering their important advantages. But, their presence in microgrids results in complicated protection coordination problems. This paper suggests a protection coordination scheme (PCS) in MGs, which is based on dual setting directional overcurrent relays (DOCRs) considering single outage contingency. In this paper, the conventional and dual setting DOCR-based PCSs are compared in two steps, without and with considering the single outage contingency, respectively. It is shown that in complex and practical cases, the advantages of the dual setting based PCS is more obvious. To reveal the validity of the proposed PCS, the simulation studies are conducted based on the modified version of the IEEE 30-bus test system. Using the short circuit currents obtained by DIgSILENT, the optimization problem is solved in MATLAB environment as a mixed integer non-linear programming problem. The results show the superiority of the Dual setting PCS over the conventional PCS.

articleTitle: Synthesis of Large-Area MoS2 Sword-Like Flakes by Chemical Vapor Deposition
abstract: Recently, the emerging field of two-dimensional materials is known to be promising due to their unique structure, special optical and electrical properties, and their applications in optoelectronic devices. In this paper, for the first time, we are reporting on new MoS<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> samples with slightly different structures to that of the conventional ones. This is achieved using chemical vapor deposition (CVD) method and further changing of argon flux, furnace temperature, and precursors' distance to the location of substrates. This structure is sword-like, and it should be noted that length of some of these sword-like specimens is measured to be ≅700 micrometres. The broad dimensions of these samples may simplify the manufacturing process of the electronic components. The CVD reaction used here is carried out inside a furnace with one thermal zone and using sulfur and MoO3 as precursors. By changing the three effective growth parameters: argon flux, scraping the substrate surface (silicon oxide), and synthesis time, an optimum condition for the growth of the sword specimens is obtained. It is found that increasing argon flux up to a specific limit (200 SCCM), increases the length of the sword specimens, however, passing this limit, the length of the sword samples will stop increasing. Scratching the substrate's surface causes the sword-like specimens to accumulate in the scratched region. Furthermore, increasing the synthesis time results in the growth of more samples on the substrate's surface and creates a change in the samples crystalline form and transforms them into the fractal-like structure.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of Class-F3/E2 Power Amplifier using Shunt Filter for Satellite Communication
abstract: In this paper, the switchmode Class-F3/E2 power amplifier with transmission lines at 2.21 GHz is discussed and simulated. The aim is to obtain high efficiency using even and odd harmonic control circuits. The dimensions of the load network are dependent upon the desired specifications and obtained by explicit equations. The simulated maximum drain efficiency of the main stage is 85%, and power added efficiency is 72%. Also, output power of 47 W is obtained at 25 dBm input power.

articleTitle: Identifying the most influential communities on the dissemination of information on social networks
abstract: Many people receive and adopt ideas and opinions using their connections in social networks, which facilitate accessibility and spreading of information. Homophily in interests speeds up the adoption of the information spreading process. Communities provide a coarse grain representative of network users with common interests. Here, we address the effects of community structures on the virality of information in social networks. We use real data sets of the Twitter network, and we show that in many viral hashtags, some communities characterized by a high ratio of inter-connections to intra-connection have appeared at the initial stages of meme adaptation. We show that the adoption of a hashtag in these communities can cause the attention of a broader audience, and this can cause virality. This result suggests that the spreading of an idea can be boosted up if that opinion implants in these communities and these communities adopt the idea.

articleTitle: Simultaneous design of $H_{2}$ controller and observer in the presence of disturbance for linear systems
abstract: In this work, we design a simultaneous H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> controller and a state observer for linear systems in the presence of disturbance using linear matrix inequality (LMI) technique. A linear state feedback is proposed to stabilize the states of the control system. In addition, the problem of stabilizing the system states and optimizing the observer design by computing H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> is combined with the linear matrix inequality method. After obtaining state controller and observer values using LMI and applying them to the system, it is observed that stability and performance of the closed loop system against disturbance are guaranteed. The simulation results of two numerical examples are presented to show the effectiveness and feasibility of the presented method in this article.

articleTitle: Investigation of Bismuth Doping Effects on CZTS Properties: A Density Functional Theory Study
abstract: Post-transition metal-doped quaternary chalcopyrite CZTS film has been proposed as a novel approach to improve solar energy capturing and conversion strategy. In this paper, lattice structural and optical properties of CZTS (Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>ZnSnS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>) in pure and Bi-doped conditions are theoretically investigated by employing first-principle density functional theory (DFT). Results indicate that lattice constant and bonding lengths do not change after adding bismuth substitution for a tin site. Projected density of states has been calculated for sulfur atoms on the first layer of adjacent Bismuth. Hybridization occurs between 6p state of bismuth and 3s state of sulfur atom. Furthermore, the PDOS diagram represents energy bandgap of 0.7eV and Fermi energy shift to the conduction band edge. An acceptor state is induced due to bismuth-tin substitution about 0.5 eV above the valance band edge. According to optical results extracting from dielectric functions, the absorption coefficient for bismuth-doped structure increases to 5.5×10<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>cm<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</inf> for low energy photons whereas, pure CZTS has no absorbed photon in this range. A slight decrement is exhibited in visible light reflection. Due to the acceptor state, the conductivity of carrier is facilitated for lower energy photons. Consequently, the substitution between bismuth and tin improved optical properties of CZTS as an absorber layer.

articleTitle: Pd@TiO2 Core-Shell Nanoparticles Supported by Graphite Carbon Nitride Nanosheets as a Sensitive Ethanol Sensor
abstract: Herein, we report the construction of a sensitive ethanol sensor based on palladium (Pd)@ titanium oxide (TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) core-shell nanoparticles supported by graphite carbon nitride (g-C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>) nanosheets synthesized by the combination of the facile hydrothermal process and calcination method. The structural and morphological features of the synthesized material were characterized. Transmission electron microscopy analysis showed that the Pd nanoparticles as cores are surrounded by TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> shell and anchored onto the g-C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> nanosheets. The response of the sensor towards ethanol was examined by electrical resistance measurement. The results of gas sensing performance reveal that the Pd@TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>/g-C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> sensor has a great response to ethanol at a low operating temperature of 125°C with a response and recovery times of about 30 s and 15 s, respectively. It was observed that the response of the sensor increased almost linearly with increasing ethanol concentration from 50 ppm to 1000 ppm. The high response of Pd@TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>/g-C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> can be ascribed to the Schottky junction formed between the Pd and TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and the high surface area of g-C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>.

articleTitle: Sensitivity Enhancement of Ion Sensitive Field Effect Transistor with High Mobility Semiconductor through TCAD Simulation
abstract: This paper introduces high mobility semiconductors to increase ion sensitive field effect transistor (ISFET) sensitivity to hydrogen concentration (pH) in electrolyte. The ISFET principle of operation based on electrolyte-insulator-semiconductor structure is explained, while SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> is used as the sensing film in the proposed device. Simulation results show that ISFET synthesis using GaAs as the semiconductor substrate has in average 2.3 times more sensitivity to pH variation in comparison with ISFET using Si as the semiconductor substrate.

articleTitle: Optimization-based design of fractional order PID controller: the exchange market algorithm
abstract: Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) controllers are known to be widely industrially used in spite of their conventionality. The generalization of them has resulted in more desirable controllers called Fractional Order Proportional-Integral-Derivative (FOPID) controllers only with the difficulty of tuning more number of parameters. In this paper, a tuning approach is presented to determine the parameters by the Exchange Market Algorithm (EMA), to optimize time domain features in a cost function. To the authors' knowledge, this algorithm is used to tune FOPID controllers for the first time. Furthermore, the superiority of the FOPID controllers over the PID controllers is demonstrated by applying them to control three standard functions. The results are simulated by MATLAB and evaluated in time domain represented in step responses.

articleTitle: Johnson $\mathrm{S}_{U}$ distribution in Dispersion Managed Coherent Optical OFDM Transmission Systems
abstract: In this paper, signal components after propagation in a dispersion managed (DM) coherent optical fiber link are analyzed, statistically. In this way, the received signal Gaussianity is investigated using two Gaussian tests, the Anderson-Darling and the Jarque-Bera. Deviation from Gaussian distribution is result of increasing the launch power, that is measured by the tests. Next, we use Johnson S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">U</sub> distribution for distribution fitting and show its good approximation in DM systems. Bit error rate (BER) is employed for performance evaluation that is calculated in three methods: 1) Gaussian based, 2) Johnson SU based, and, 3) Monte-Carlo (MC) simulations based on the split-step Fourier method. It is demonstrated that in the nonlinear region, using Johnson S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">U</sub> distribution will have about 2 dB better power prediction than Gaussian in BER=10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup>, and the performance fits to the MC method with more accuracy.

articleTitle: Blind Detection of BCH Length from Noisy Received Vectors
abstract: In this paper, the goal is the length detection of BCH codes from noisy vectors received through a Binary Symmetric Channel (BSC) with cross over probability τ. The proposed method seeks to recover the length of code based on linear properties of cyclic codes. The received bitstream is divided into different likely lengths, and the algorithm puts the divided vector and its shifts in distinct rows of a matrix A. The rank of Λ is calculated, and detector makes a decision based on the rank value, while the rank of the matrix which contains codewords cannot exceed the length of message k /. Therefore, minimum rank is chosen as a sign of linear properties and codewords space. The operation is practical because of the low complexity of calculating the rank, and it can be done over GF(2) and modulo 2 addition.

articleTitle: Zero Forcing Transceiver Design for uplink of MultiUser CGFDMA Systems
abstract: In generalized frequency division multiplexing (GFDM) technique, the data symbols are transmitted on different time and frequency by using non-orthogonal pulse shapes. This causes two dimensional self-interference (SI) among the transmitted symbols. Recently, a modified version of GFDM, coded GFDM (CGFDM), has been introduced avoiding the noise enhancement during SI cancellation by providing a unitary SI matrix. In this paper, we generalize the CGFDM idea to be used in the uplink of a multiuser transmission scenario, and develop a zero-forcing (ZF) receiver to detect data symbols of multiple users. Simulation results show that the proposed ZF based transceiver outperforms the conventional ZF based generalized frequency division multiple access transceiver when the number of subsymbols is high and the prototype filter is less localized, with just a slight increase in computation complexity.

articleTitle: Persian Document Classification Using Deep Learning Methods
abstract: Currently, the classification issue of Persian articles is sparse, limited, and non-automatic. So, information can be extracted from the structure of web pages that aids in the usual way of classifying texts. Text words are usually used as text features in text classification. As a result, text classification methods have many features. Numerous methods are used to reduce the number of features and to select related features. Based on deep learning, this paper proposes methods for extracting features of Persian texts, methods for classifying texts and finally identifying the subject matter of the collection. In this paper, the Hamshahri dataset (a sub-body containing 166,000 documents with a specific theme), one of the most prestigious Persian language resources in the field of natural language, is applied for feature extraction and text classification. The results of this paper indicate that the implementation of the classification of Persian news texts has achieved satisfactory performance.

articleTitle: An Improved Salp Swarm Algorithm for energy saving in IoT to FOG data communication
abstract: In recent years, through the rapid progress of the Internet of Things technology, minimizing the energy consumption of smart nodes in wireless communication is one of the major challenges in this area. Due to the large number of sensor nodes, which are powered by limited capacity batteries, it is impractical to replace or recharge their batteries. The major energy consumption of smart nodes is related to their network communication; therefore, optimum utilization of energy stored in each smart node is an important aspect of the IoT regarding their durability. In this paper, we suggest an Improved version of the Salp Swarm Algorithm (ISSA) for solving the problem of energy consumption in the IoT network by finding an optimal routing for transmission of smart nodes data to the FOG. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm outperforms rival algorithms by a 16.4% improvement in energy consumption.

articleTitle: Systematic Structure to Implement the Retiming Algorithm as a GUI Software
abstract: In this paper, a systematic structure to implement the retiming algorithm as a software is proposed. Using this structure, a software which performs the retiming algorithm automatically from a graphical input is presented. Through this software the input digital system is modeled in the computer, then it is converted to a predefined matrix format, finally the software performs the retiming algorithm to minimize the Critical Path (CP). Next, the software delivers the retimed system as a graphical schematic. The software is designed as a Graphical User Interface (GUI) and it is tested for many sample digital systems. Simulation results show the proposed software provides a simple fast system optimization. In fact, users are able to quickly draw their digital systems in the software then perform the retiming algorithm. Generally, this paper describes how to systematically create a GUI based software from an advanced algorithm for a user so that the user does not need to learn about the base theory or mathematical formats for interpreting both the inputs and the results; he/she just employs the software using simple graphical actions such as mouse/keyboard clicking.

articleTitle: Robust stabilization of a class of switched nonlinear systems with time-varying delay and parametric uncertainty under asynchronous switching
abstract: This paper addresses the robust stabilization issue of switched systems with the essence of model uncertainties, time-varying delay, and nonlinear terms under asynchronous switching. The Lyapunov-Krasovskii functional approach and an average dwell time technique are utilized to establish sufficient conditions to compute the gains of a stabilizing switched controller. Obtained conditions are converted to linear matrix inequalities (LM/s) which rely on the upper bounds of the switching time lag between the system modes activation and the corresponding controller modes, the time-varying state delay, and the parameter uncertainties. A numerical example is allocated to validate the efficacy of the proposed strategy.

articleTitle: Image Quality Improvement in Single Pixel IR-Imaging
abstract: We have implemented a single-pixel passive imaging system to be used in the infrared range of radiation. The output of the proposed system is under the influence of several disturbing factors. We identified these factors, and modelled their associated noise and distortions theoretically based on which we reduced the effects of these perturbations in the experiment. We described the effect of the thermal noise by covering the system. Also, the size of the aperture was decreased such that only the first order of diffracted wave was received by the sensor. And finally, we used image processing techniques to improve the quality of the image.

articleTitle: Caching Placement and Offloading in D2D-Assisted Wireless Networks with In-Band Full Duplex
abstract: In this paper, we propose a new approach for maximizing the benefits of device-to-device (D2D) communication with cache memory as well as the caching placement and delivery content. To this end, caching placement, scheduling policies, and in-band full duplex (IBFD) are used to maximize the offloading probability, defined as the probability of obtaining the desired content by user. Each user can obtain its content in a local memory or through a helper cache (node that only has memory capacity) or a D2D communications link. A scheduling policy is used to prevent and control interference from D2D in the distribution method. The mode of choice between Half-Duplex (HD) and IBFD with a fixed probability in device-to-device communication is considered. The results show that our proposed approach, compared to related work, leads to an improvement in the offloading probability.

articleTitle: Comparative study of crosstalk noise and delay in MLGNR and Cu interconnects
abstract: Multi-layer graphene nanoribbons are one of the most probable successive materials for replacing Cu interconnects in very large scale integrated circuit. In this work the crosstalk induced noise and delay in MLGNR and Cu based interconnects are analytically calculated and compared. It is shown that MLGNR interconnects can outperform Cu ones in terms of crosstalk delay provided the surface of underlying substrate material is smooth enough.
